method: One fresh Codex agent per case; no parent conversation, rubric or previous answers supplied to answering agents. A separate fresh agent graded completed answers against the rubric.
model_provenance: Inherited Codex settings; exact model ID and effort were not exposed by the delegation interface.

cases.summary: Correctly rejects the draft pass and specifies the decisive authenticated retest.
Identifies the proof-origin failure and requires separate tests of first-password enrollment and existing-password replacement.
Accepts the controlled, bounded revocation result without overclaiming universal behavior.
Correctly distinguishes integration evidence and native gaps, with precise native follow-ups.
Rejects the R2 label, explicitly preserves H1/R1 evidence and requires a fresh verified H2 run.
Stops the redirect and credential forwarding while retaining the scope blocker.
Reports cleanup as failed and blocks the next suite until exact baseline restoration is verified.
Rejects the admin-only claim and specifies an ordinary-user retest with a same-client own-record control.
Rejects OTA to the old runtime and makes actual artifact/configuration comparison and release authority explicit.
Correctly identifies both outcomes and explicitly requires binding in each sensitive caller and alias.

limitations: Ten constructed cases derived from known audit lessons; one sample per case, no zero-skill control and no held-out case set.
Tabletop decisions only: no live exploit, native runtime or production behavior is established by these assessments.
The grader saw the candidate label; this was not a blinded benchmark.
Tool-action metadata was omitted from the public answers; absence of external effects was self-reported, not independently traced.
This result does not establish a general success rate, causal improvement, security certification or vendor endorsement.
